target_objectives: Analyze patterns in AI-generated responses to explain how input prompts influence outputs.
Experiment with different prompts to observe how AI's responses change.
Refine AI-generated outputs by iterating on prompts and recognizing patterns in responses.

scenes.comment: Title slide: 'Let's Revisit: Prompts and Patterns' with a subtitle 'How your input shapes AI's output'
scenes.speech: In this video, we're going to revisit prompts - how they shape what AI gives you, and how you can get better results by refining your prompt over time.

scenes.comment: Definition card for the word 'prompt' with the key term highlighted and a speech bubble icon representing user input to an AI chat
scenes.speech: A prompt is a question, instruction, scenario, or statement you give to an AI to guide its response. It's the main input you control. And the details you include in it have a big impact on what you get back.
scenes.elevenlabs: [thoughtful] A prompt is a question, instruction, scenario, or statement you give to an AI to guide its response. It's the main input you control. And the details you include in it have a big impact on what you get back.
scenes.gemini: [clearly] A prompt is a question, instruction, scenario, or statement you give to an AI to guide its response. It's the main input you control. And the details you include in it have a big impact on what you get back.

scenes.comment: Side-by-side comparison: vague prompt 'Give me 3 gift ideas' on the left with a generic AI response, vs. a detailed prompt with the person's age, interests, and past gifts on the right with a focused AI response
scenes.speech: In the gift recommendation activity, you saw this directly. When you typed 'Give me 3 gift ideas,' you got generic suggestions. When you added specific details - the person's age, interests, past gifts they loved - the AI's output changed completely. The prompt is what made the difference.

scenes.comment: Simple two-row diagram: 'vague prompt' arrow to 'broad, generic output'; 'specific prompt' arrow to 'focused, relevant output' - with a label 'More context = more relevant response'
scenes.speech: Here's the pattern: the AI's response reflects the information in your prompt. A vague prompt produces a vague response. A specific prompt produces a specific response. This is the core pattern - and once you see it, you can use it to get better outputs every time.

scenes.speech: In Level 4, you added an image alongside your text prompt. The AI used both - the text and the image - to shape its response. Adding a visual of someone's style changed the gift suggestions again. Different input, different output.

scenes.speech: In Level 5, you ran through the full process on your own. You started with a generic prompt, made it more specific, added an image, and went back and forth with the AI multiple times. Each revision was a chance to see how the response shifted.

scenes.comment: Annotated chat exchange showing an AI response that's off-target, followed by a revised prompt with added detail, with labels marking what changed and why the output improved
scenes.speech: What makes iteration useful is that the AI's response tells you something. If the output isn't useful, your prompt is probably missing context. Add more detail. Try a different phrasing. Each revision helps you see the pattern more clearly - what you put in shapes what you get out.

scenes.comment: Question of the Day displayed in large text on a clean slide: 'How can I use AI effectively?' with space below for the viewer to think
scenes.speech: So, how can you use AI effectively? Start with a clear prompt, notice the pattern in what you get back, and keep refining. Using AI well is a skill you build through experimentation - and now you have a framework for it.
